title: fix(spec): NormalizedFilterSchema judges its `$and`/`$or`/`$not` members instead of catching them all (#7711)
body:
Fixes #7711

## What was wrong

Each `$and` / `$or` member and the `$not` operand of `NormalizedFilterSchema` was:

```ts
z.union([
  z.record(z.string(), FieldOperatorsSchema),  // field condition
  NormalizedFilterSchema,                      // nested logical group
])
```

and the second branch is a NON-strict `z.object({ $and, $or, $not })` with every key
optional. "All three of my optional keys are absent" is true of any object whatsoever, so
that branch was a **catch-all**: whenever the record branch *rejected* a field condition,
the group branch accepted the very same value. The whole-filter face validated the logical
skeleton and nothing else — no comparand shape it declares could ever make it fail, while
its own comments say it is what enforces `FieldOperatorsSchema`.

Re-measured on the current `origin/main` @ `8669e5d` (post-#7713), and the card's anchors
hold. Every row below was green:

| input | `NormalizedFilterSchema.safeParse` before | parse OUTPUT before | `FieldOperatorsSchema` on the same operator map |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `{ $and: [{ c: { $null: 'not-a-boolean' } }] }` | `true` | `{ $and: [{}] }` | `false` |
| `{ $and: [{ c: { $between: [1, 2, 3] } }] }` | `true` | `{ $and: [{}] }` | `false` |
| `{ $and: [{ c: { $between: [{ $field: 'b' }, 100] } }] }` | `true` | `{ $and: [{}] }` | `false` |
| `{ $and: [{ hello: 'world' }] }` | `true` | `{ $and: [{}] }` | n/a |
| `{ $and: [{ $not: { c: { $null: 'nope' } } }] }` | `true` | `{ $and: [{ $not: {} }] }` | `false` |
| `{ c: { $null: 'nope' } }` (top level) | `true` | `{}` | `false` |

The **output column** is the part the card had not measured and it decided the fix over
option 3 (delete the "ENFORCED" claim from the comments): the green was also **lossy** —
whatever the catch-all admitted came back parsed to `{}`, so the accepted output no longer
carried the condition it was asked about. A whole `{ $not: … }` subtree parsed as a field
NAMED `$not` and returned empty.

## The fix

Issue options 1 and 2 together, because neither alone closes it:

- the group branch is `.strict()`, so a field condition cannot slip past as an empty
  logical group;
- the field-condition branch rules out `$`-prefixed keys, which is what discriminates the
  union. `FieldOperatorsSchema` is deliberately not `.strict()`, so `{ c: … }` read as an
  operator map has every key stripped and returns `{}` — that is how `{ $not: … }`
  used to answer on the field-condition branch and never reach the group branch at all.

The refusal is message-bearing per lane convention, riding on the union's own `error`
callback (the idiom `rangeEndpointSchema` uses two hundred lines up):

```
Not a valid $and member — got an object with key(s) "c". A $and member is either a FIELD
CONDITION ({ "field": { "$op": value } }, whose keys are field names and whose operator map
must satisfy FieldOperatorsSchema — comparand shapes included), or a nested LOGICAL GROUP
carrying only $and / $or / $not and nothing else. Ruled on #7711: declared = enforced
(ADR-0049).
```

The field-branch refinement carries `abort: true`. Measured on zod 4.4.3: a union whose
other options all abort returns a lone CONTINUABLE failure verbatim, which made
`{ $not: { c: … } }` — a legitimate group shape with a bad operand — report "keys are
field names", blaming `$not` for being spelled at all. Aborting keeps the union's own
message in charge of every rejection.

**Deliberately still accepted**: the #5322 empty-combinator identities — `{}`,
`{ $and: [] }`, `{ $or: [] }`, `{ $or: [{}] }`, `{ $not: {} }`. `{}` reaches the
field-condition branch as an empty record, which is exactly what lets the group branch be
strict without touching any of them. Each is pinned.

The one shape the strictness might have cost — a group key and a field key at one level,
`{ $or: [], c: { $eq: 1 } }` — is a **non-loss**: it parsed to `{ $or: [] }` before, the
field condition dropped on the floor, so no mixed member ever survived a round-trip.

## Blast radius — measured, zero

- **No runtime caller.** Nothing in the repo calls `.parse` / `.safeParse` on
  `NormalizedFilterSchema` outside `packages/spec`'s own tests. Positive control for the
  sweep: the same grep over `FilterConditionSchema` returns 20-plus call sites across
  `packages/spec`, `service-analytics` and `metadata-protocol`, so the search does find
  callers when they exist.
- **Cross-path check (requested on the card).** The drivers and the evaluator consume the
  LOWERED `FilterCondition`, never this AST: `driver-memory` 16 files / `driver-sql` 21 /
  `driver-mongodb` 3 / `driver-sqlite-wasm` 3 / `driver-turso` 6 reference
  `FilterCondition`, and **0** of them reference `NormalizedFilter`; same for
  `packages/formula` (12 / 0) and `packages/objectql` (9 / 0). `service-analytics`'s
  `NormalizedFilterNode` is its own local discriminated-union type in
  `strategies/filter-normalizer.ts`, unrelated to spec's `NormalizedFilter`. So this
  schema-door tightening cannot diverge any row set.
- **The exported type is unchanged.** `NormalizedFilter` is byte-identical; every shape
  that stops parsing was already outside it. `NormalizedFilterSchema`'s
  `z.ZodType< NormalizedFilter, NormalizedFilter >` annotation is unchanged too.

## Changeset grade

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, following the two strict-unknown-keys precedents
(`action-param-strict-unknown-keys`, `action-strict-envelope-zero` — both `minor`). Not
the #7657 / ADR-0087 `major` grade: nothing is REMOVED from the declared surface here, the
exported type does not move, and the shapes that stop parsing are produced by nothing —
there is no normalizer in the repo emitting this AST and no consumer reading it.

## Tests

- **Flip-don't-delete.** #7713's looseness-control pin
  (`the whole-filter face is loose about field conditions — pre-existing, control
  included`) is flipped in place, not deleted: same two inputs, same two
  `FieldOperatorsSchema` assertions (unchanged — that level always rejected both), and the
  pair that moved is the whole-filter verdict. Its docblock now records what the case was
  originally written to pin and why it flipped.
- New `#7711` describe block: 8 cases covering each slot, the nested case, the
  `$not`-as-a-field-name leak, non-field-condition members, top-level unknown keys, the
  #5322 identities staying green, and the output-preservation side (a `$not` subtree is no
  longer erased).
- Rejections assert the issue `code` and `path` plus the message's load-bearing spans, not
  just `success === false`.

**Reverse verification** (direction predicted before running — "red, the usual"; taken out
with `git checkout origin/main -- the file` against a checkpoint commit, never `git stash`):
removing `filter.zod.ts`'s change turned **exactly 8** cases red in `filter.test.ts` — the
7 new pins plus the flipped #7713 control — and the identities case stayed green, which is
the case that must not depend on the fix. Restored: 136/136 green.

## Gates run locally

| gate | result |
| :--- | :--- |
| `@objectstack/spec` filter suites (9 files) | 309 passed |
| `@objectstack/spec` full `vitest run` | 9955 tests, green after regenerating the strictness-ledger counts |
| `@objectstack/spec` `typecheck` (tsc + scripts + test-typecheck) | green |
| `pnpm check:driver-conformance` | OK — 38 covered cells, 2 in DEBT, 0 exempt |
| `pnpm check:merge-driver` | self-tests pass |
| `pnpm check:adr-anchors` | OK — 22384 citations across 3690 files resolve |
| `pnpm check:spec-parsed-alias` | OK — ADR-0122 convention |
| `pnpm check:nul-bytes` | OK — 7128 files, no raw control bytes |
| `@objectstack/spec` `check:generated` | all 13 artifacts up to date |
| `@objectstack/spec` `check:authorable-surface` | green; `authorable-surface.base.json` unchanged by the rebuild |
| downstream `@objectstack/objectql` typecheck | green (dep closure built with the `^...` SUFFIX first) |

Consumer-sweep direction, stated so the line can be reviewed: this is **not** the full
prefix sweep (`--filter '...@objectstack/spec'` is effectively the whole repo). It is
spec's own typecheck plus one targeted downstream consumer, justified by the exported type
being unchanged — the runtime narrowing has no caller to sweep for.

## Generated artifact moved with the change

`docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts.md` — `filter.zod.ts` strip sites
11 → 10, repo-wide strip 181 → 180, strict 251 → 252. Regenerated with
`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:strictness-ledger`, i.e. the campaign ledger records
this as one site closed.

## Scope

`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`, the `NormalizedFilterSchema` union region only.
The `$between` / `$in` / `$nin` unions and `parseFilterAST` are untouched — both settled
today by #7713 / #7672. The two "this copy is the ENFORCED one" comments inside
`FieldOperatorsSchema` are left exactly as they are: they sit in the settled `$between`
neighbourhood, and they are now simply TRUE, which is what the issue asked for. The
argument they used to gloss over lives in this schema's own docblock instead.
